Foundation / Color

Color

Single brand orange, role names with a numbered ramp underneath. The palette is anchored by one accent — #F24E1E. Everything else flips with section mode. Role-named tokens are the canonical references; the numbered ramp sits underneath for design-token tools and Figma variable parity. Both names point at the same value.

Brand

Brand orange leads every focal action — the only saturated hue in the system. Hover uses a deeper tone from the same ramp. Error red is reserved for destructive and invalid states only.

Text tokens

Two scales — one per surface — with five contrast levels each. Direct hex use is forbidden; everything reads from these tokens.

On darkValueUse
--text-on-dark100%Display, primary text, button labels
--text-on-dark-display95%Display headings (slight lift off pure white)
--text-on-dark-muted75%Body, lead, descriptions
--text-on-dark-subtle65%Helper text, label-on-card meta
--text-on-dark-second60%Two-tone headline second clause
On lightValueUse
--text-on-light100% (#111111)Display, primary text, button labels
--text-on-light-display90%Display headings
--text-on-light-muted75%Body, lead, descriptions
--text-on-light-subtle60%Helper text, label-on-card meta
--text-on-light-second65%Two-tone headline second clause

Text contracts (accessibility-tested floors)

  • Body on dark: minimum white at 75% (primary) or 65% (utility).
  • Body on light: minimum #111 at 75% (primary) or 60% (utility).
  • Display headings can sit at 90–95% opacity.
  • Decorative chrome (dot patterns, hairlines, fade gradients): 25–35% — never for readable glyphs.
  • Brand orange on body text fails AA. Never use orange for body — accent surfaces and CTAs only.

Usage

Read from tokens; never use raw hex in markup or component CSS. Surface flips work because every component binds to scoped variables that rebind under .bk-section--dark / .bk-section--light / .is-flipped-*.

Atoms / Button

Button

* What changed in v2.1 Mobile min-height: var(--touch-target-min, 44px) on every variant — CRITICAL accessibility fix per Apple HIG / WCAG (was effectively ~38–40px on ghost-dark in some surfaces). The --touch-target-min token already existed; v2.1 just enforces it.

Pill-shaped action triggers. One primary per viewport; secondary and ghost handle paired CTAs and tertiary actions. All variants share label-md text, 9999px radius, and 44px minimum touch target. Stateful variants (disabled, loading) and editorial variants (arrow-circle CTA, anchor pill) live on this page too.

Primary

The focal action. Brand orange fill, white label. One per viewport — competing primaries dilute attention. The orange reads with equal weight on either surface; the fill / label colors don't change between dark and light.

on-dark
on-light

Secondary

Paired-CTA alternate. Subtle filled background that recedes against the primary. Renders correctly on either surface via dark/light variants.

on-dark
on-light

Ghost

Tertiary actions and inline links. Outlined, no filled background; subtle dark/light tint on hover.

on-dark
on-light

Ghost · on-charcoal

The in-card ghost variant. When a ghost sits inside a charcoal card on a dark surface, the standard ghost-dark's border reads too hot — this variant softens it. Used in pricing cards, project tiles, and any nested charcoal surface.

Icon-only

40×40 visible bound; hit area extends to 44×44 via a transparent ::after. Always carries aria-label.

on-dark
on-light

Disabled

Inactive state — pointer-events suppressed, 40% opacity. Always pair a disabled button with helper text or a tooltip explaining why; an unexplained dead button is a UX dead end. Use disabled for form submits, aria-disabled="true" for anchors that need to remain in tab order.

on-dark
on-light

Loading

Async-action state. Replace the leading icon with a spinner; keep the label so screen-readers don't lose their place. Mark with aria-busy="true" and disabled so pointer + keyboard both block a double-submit.

on-dark
on-light

Success on submit

Use for form submits that need inline confirmation. The demo hook runs the full sequence: Sending + spinner, then Thank you + check icon, then reset to the original label. Production code should trigger the success step only after the request resolves.

on-dark
on-light

Arrow-circle CTA

Editorial link variant. Uppercase mono label paired with an orange circle holding an arrow. The signature "Learn more →" pattern that bridges body copy to a deeper-dive surface — used in section closers, content cards, and lifecycle stages.

on-dark Learn more
on-light Learn more

Anchor pill

Inline editorial link variant. Lightweight outlined pill for inline cross-links — calmer than a button, more visible than a plain text link.

on-dark Engineering
on-light Engineering

Usage rules

One primary per viewport. Two primaries in the same screen competing for attention dilutes the orange.

Pill always. All buttons use 9999px radius. No exceptions — never a hard-cornered button.

Min 44px touch target. Below 44×44 fails WCAG 2.5.5 on touch devices. Icon-only buttons hit this via ::after expansion.

Disabled needs explanation. Never ship a dead button with no context — pair it with helper text or a tooltip so the user knows why it can't be clicked.

Loading blocks double-submit. The async pattern is aria-busy="true" + disabled together, so neither pointer nor keyboard can re-fire the action.

Organisms / Modal

Modal

Generic dialog with backdrop blur + lift shadow. Three layers — backdrop (full-viewport blur + dim), dialog box (charcoal/white, 16px radius, soft lift), close affordance (white circle below the modal, visible and reachable). The previews below show the modal inline-stage; production places it via position: fixed; inset: 0 with body-scroll-lock on open.

Variant A · Action modal

01 · Action modal
One focal decision. Primary + Ghost button pair at the bottom-right. The user is being asked to commit to or back out of an irreversible-ish action.

on-dark

Switch workspace?

You'll exit the current indexing session. Any pending uploads will continue in the background and surface in the new workspace's recent items.

on-light

Switch workspace?

You'll exit the current indexing session. Any pending uploads will continue in the background and surface in the new workspace's recent items.

Variant B · Info modal

02 · Info modal
Single dismiss — read and close. No commitment, no decision. Brief context with a single close action. Used for release notes, compliance disclosures, "what's new" banners.

on-dark
V2.4 · Release note

RTStream is now generally available

Live agent-controlled playback over a video index. Sub-second latency, available in every region. No code changes required for existing pipelines.

on-light
V2.4 · Release note

RTStream is now generally available

Live agent-controlled playback over a video index. Sub-second latency, available in every region. No code changes required for existing pipelines.

Variant C · Form modal

03 · Form modal
Input required — modal as the form surface. Used when a flow is gated by user input that doesn't warrant its own page. Enquiry forms, invite-team, "request access" patterns. Composes the modal recipe with the multi-field Form field pattern.

on-dark

Tell us about your project

We'll route your enquiry to the right team and respond within one business day.

on-light

Tell us about your project

We'll route your enquiry to the right team and respond within one business day.

Usage rules

Three intent variants only. CTA drives a decision; Info acknowledges a state; Form captures input. Don't invent a fourth — if you need something else, you're using a modal where a page or inline disclosure belongs.

Close affordance lives outside the modal. The white circle below the dialog is intentional — it's reachable on touch (away from the modal's edge) and reads as a discrete affordance, not chrome. Esc + backdrop click also close.

Body-scroll-lock on open. The page underneath shouldn't scroll while the modal is open. Production code adds overflow: hidden to <body> and restores on close.

Focus management. First focusable input receives focus ~100ms after open (so the open animation finishes first). On close, focus returns to the trigger element.

Composed from atoms + molecules. Button for the action pair, Input + Field label for the form variant, Form field for multi-field arrangements.

Foundation / Typography

Typography

* What changed in v2.1 Added .ds-section-heading__title responsive clamp: font-size: clamp(26px, 4.5vw, 40px) (was a fixed 40px). New --display modifier with clamp(32px, 5vw, 56px) for hero-adjacent section titles. Mobile .ds-section-heading__lead drops 18→16px.

Geist + JetBrains Mono. Two families. Single-family discipline for everything readable — Geist carries display, body, UI; JetBrains Mono is reserved for technical chrome (section codes, eyebrow labels, code blocks, bracketed labels).

Critical rules

  • text-wrap: balance on every display class — eliminates widow lines automatically.
  • font-family: 'Geist', sans-serif set explicitly on every display class (defeats Tailwind preflight's h1–h6 reset).
  • line-height: !important on every display class (defeats Tailwind's bundled text-{size} utility line-heights).
  • display-md line-height locked at 1.15 — anything below reintroduces descender collisions on two-tone <br>-split headings.
  • Two-tone declarative headings (preferred when copy has a rhetorical break) use a single text run + <br> + <span>. Never stacked <div> blocks.

Foundation / Layout

Layout

* What changed in v2.1 New 6-tier mobile breakpoint canon (custom properties): --bp-xs 420, --bp-sm 640, --bp-md 768, --bp-lg 960, --bp-xl 1280, --bp-2xl 1440. .ds-frame side-borders dropped below 640px (rail aesthetic doesn't read on phones). html, body now use overflow-x: clip (NOT hidden — hidden creates a scrollport that breaks position: sticky).

1400 px frame, five canonical breakpoints, two-tier column offset. A centred 1400px column with 1px vertical hairlines on either side, persisting through every section. Sections alternate dark ↔ light, full commitment per section.

Breakpoints — five tiers, mobile-first

TokenWidthUse
--bp-sm640pxSmall phone → larger phone. Typography sometimes steps here.
--bp-md768pxMobile → tablet. Primary break. Container padding 16→24, first 2-up grids open.
--bp-lg1024pxTablet → desktop. Multi-column section layouts unlock.
--bp-xl1280pxDesktop. Pricing tier finder full-width; multi-column footer.
--bp-2xl1400pxMax content width. Pairs with --max-content.

Column offset — two-tier rule

Strict 2/10 at the section opener; large interactives can opt-in to .full-bleed-content inside the right column.

Section-opener tier (default)

Every section, light or dark: section code in left col (md:col-span-3 lg:col-span-2), content in right col (md:col-span-9 lg:col-span-10 max-w-5xl). Heading + lead use 8/4 split inside the right column.

Container tier (opt-in)

Inside the right column, large interactive containers MAY fill the full 10-column width via the .full-bleed-content modifier. Applies to: code blocks, hero feature surfaces, lifecycle flows, comparison tables wider than 8/4, pricing tier finder, carousels, tickers.

Section modes — Dark ↔ Light

ModeBackgroundRailUse
Dark#0A0A0Aborder-on-dark-strongHero, product / platform sections, code-led messaging, atmospheric moments
Light#F5F5F7border-on-light-strongEditorial, content-forward, pricing, FAQ, testimonials, dense reading

Sections alternate deliberately to create scroll rhythm. Don't blend modes within one section — pick and commit.

Dual-radius rounded vocabulary. Five tokens, role-disciplined. Surfaces are rounded by default — the only square-cornered elements in the system are decorative hairlines (frame borders, section dividers) and the dotted-pattern badge's inner field. Do not introduce sharp-1px components.

Foundation / Motion

Motion

Three categories, three sets of rules. Decorative motion caps at 200ms. Functional motion is exempt — the animation IS the component. Ambient motion is narrowly exempt for three named cases: WebGL hero, masked word reveal, ticker. Every motion respects prefers-reduced-motion: reduce.

Decorative motion · ≤200ms cap

TriggerBehaviourDurationEasing
Button hoverBackground / colour shift150ms--ease-ui
Button active pressscale(0.985)96ms--ease-ui
Tooltip enteropacity + translateY(4→0)200ms--ease-ui
Nav-dropdown panel revealopacity + translateY(-4→0)200ms--ease-ui
Tabs panel swapopacity + translateX(20→0)220ms--ease-out
Modal enteropacity + scale(0.96→1)200ms--ease-ui

Functional motion · exempt

ComponentBehaviourDuration / cycle
Status dot pulseopacity 0.4 ↔ 11.2s loop
Inline spinnerrotation800ms / 360°
Skeleton shimmergradient sweep1.6s loop
Dot loaderframe-by-frame120–220ms / frame
Sent state ink-growclip-path circle(0% → 130%)540ms
Buzz invalid inputhorizontal shake360ms one-shot

Ambient motion · narrowly exempt

ComponentBehaviourDuration / cycle
Masked word reveal on section headingsGSAP word-by-word entrance, once on scroll~1000ms / heading, staggered
Typing code blockcharacter-by-character + cursor blinkscroll-triggered, once
WebGL hero — primary breathing domeparticle field rotation + breathcontinuous, slow · see Motion / Particle dome
Ticker (auto-scroll)translateX(0 → -50%)60s linear · hover + offscreen pause

Scroll reveal · system-wide entrance pattern

One sanctioned scroll-triggered entrance animation for the entire system. Elements with data-ds-reveal (or auto-decorated targets like .ds-section-heading and .ds-hero) fade + translate from 12px below their resting position to in-place when they enter the viewport at 12% threshold. One-shot per element — once revealed, stays revealed; no re-trigger on scroll-back-up. prefers-reduced-motion: reduce skips the animation entirely.

Specification

TokenValue
Duration400ms
Easingcubic-bezier(0.22, 1, 0.36, 1) — gentle ease-out
Initial stateopacity: 0; transform: translateY(12px)
Final stateopacity: 1; transform: translateY(0)
Trigger threshold12% intersection ratio
Root margin0px 0px -8% 0px — fire slightly before bottom of viewport
Stagger increment80ms (via data-ds-reveal-delay)
LibraryVanilla IntersectionObserver. No GSAP, no animation library.

Auto-decorated targets

On every page activation, decorateReveals() auto-adds data-ds-reveal to these classes — designers never need to mark them manually:

SelectorWhy
.ds-section-headingSection headings always benefit from a reveal moment — the entire section-heading molecule (eyebrow + h2 + lead) fades in as one unit.
.ds-heroThe hero wrapper reveals as one block: display + lead + CTA pair all in. No staggered chrome, no slideshow feel.

Opt-in usage

For elements outside the auto-targets, add the attribute explicitly. Use data-ds-reveal-delay in 80ms increments for sequenced reveals — typically a 3- or 4-up card grid:

<div class="ds-card-grid">
  <article data-ds-reveal data-ds-reveal-delay="0">...</article>
  <article data-ds-reveal data-ds-reveal-delay="80">...</article>
  <article data-ds-reveal data-ds-reveal-delay="160">...</article>
</div>

Rules

Don't decorate everything. Headlines, heroes, top-level cards in grids, big-stats blocks, hero displays. Body paragraphs, list items, button labels, table rows — never. Aggressive reveal-everywhere is the antipattern this primitive is designed to prevent.

One direction only. Always fade + translateY upward. No mixing slide-left, slide-right, scale, rotate in the same system. One primitive, one mental model.

One-shot. Observer unobserves after first reveal. Scrolling back up doesn't re-trigger — preventing the "slideshow site" antipattern.

Stagger sparingly. Reach for data-ds-reveal-delay only when the elements form a parallel set (3-up cards, 4-up stats). Don't stagger arbitrary adjacent elements. Cap stagger sequences at 4 — beyond that, the last element waits noticeably long.

Always honors reduced-motion. CSS media query forces the element to its final state with no transition. JS doesn't need to know.

Easing tokens

TokenCurveUse
--ease-uicubic-bezier(0.4, 0, 0.2, 1)Decorative UI transitions (canonical)
--ease-outcubic-bezier(0.16, 1, 0.3, 1)Decelerate — panel reveals, tab swaps, tooltip enter
--ease-revealpower4.out (GSAP)Masked word reveal
--ease-fadepower2.in/out (GSAP)Cross-fades, WebGL fade-in
--ease-springcubic-bezier(0.34, 1.56, 0.64, 1)Bounded use — sent-state check bounce only
Forbidden.

The sanctioned scroll trigger is the Scroll reveal primitive above — fade + 12px translateY, one-shot, auto-decorating headlines + heroes. No parallax. No scroll-scrub. No custom per-section entrance animations that bypass the data-ds-reveal primitive. No floating particle effects beyond the Particle dome Motion component. The page reads as engineering documentation by design.

Foundation / Iconography

Iconography

Solar via Iconify. Linear weight by default. Bold for emphasis. All icons in the system come from the Solar collection via the Iconify CDN — no SVGs in the repo. Icons inherit text color; the brand orange is reserved for surfaces and active states.

Rules

  • One icon family. Solar only. No mixing with Phosphor, Heroicons, Lucide, etc.
  • Linear weight by default. Use solar:<name>-linear.
  • Bold for emphasis. Use solar:<name>-bold for primary surface inversions (play buttons, status indicators, focal moments).
  • currentColor only. Icons inherit from parent text. Never set fill or color on an icon directly.
  • 14px default size. Icons in buttons / pills / chips render at 14×14. Standalone icons may be 18–24.
  • 40×40 hit area minimum. Icon-only buttons get a 40×40 visible bound + 44×44 hit area via ::after.

Canonical set

The Solar icons used across videodb.io. Reference, not exhaustive — any Solar icon may be used following the rules above.

Foundation / Logos & lockups

Logos & lockups

The orange V triangle is the mark. "VideoDB" is the wordmark. The composite (mark + wordmark) appears in nav, footer, and OG images. Suffix names the background the variant is built for — -dark.png for dark surfaces, -light.png for light surfaces.

Asset variants

Files

FileSurfaceUse case
assets/logos/wordmark-dark.pngdarkSite nav, footer (dark), dark hero, dark OG
assets/logos/wordmark-light.pnglightLight pricing / FAQ, light marketing collateral, light OG
assets/logos/square-dark.pngdarkSquare OG / app-icon variant for dark
assets/logos/square-light.pnglightSquare OG / app-icon variant for light
assets/logos/icon.pngany64×64 favicon

Usage rules

  • Clear space. 16 px minimum on every side. Never crowd the wordmark with adjacent text or borders.
  • Sizing. Nav brand pin: 20px tall. Footer wordmark: 24px tall. Hero / OG wordmark: 40–64px tall.
  • Pick the variant that matches the surface — never invert a variant manually.
  • The wordmark cannot be split — never strip the V triangle and use the text alone.
  • Never tile, stretch, rotate, or recolour any variant.
  • On orange / accent surfaces, the mark's internal orange should never sit on an orange background.
  • Don't apply drop shadows, glows, or filters to the logo.
  • Always use the PNG asset. Never re-render the wordmark in HTML/CSS — typesetting drift is a recurring bug.
  • In running prose write VideoDB (capital V, capital DB). The URL videodb.io keeps lowercase.

Foundation / System rules

System rules

Z-index, touch targets, browser polish. Plumbing that protects the look across iOS, Android, and pointer-only desktops. These aren't aesthetic decisions — they're hygiene.

Z-index ladder — 12 tiers, closed set

TokenValueRole · consumer
--z-base0Default document flow
--z-overlay1In-component overlays — nav-dropdown trigger pill
--z-decor2Page decoration — frame border rails
--z-mask10Surface edge masks — ticker fades
--z-dropdown20Dropdown panels — nav-dropdown · mega-menu
--z-popover30Tooltips · popovers — above dropdowns by design
--z-sticky40Sticky page chrome — nav · banner
--z-drawer50Off-canvas drawers — mobile nav (future)
--z-modal60Modal dialogs — backdrop + dialog
--z-toast70Toast notifications
--z-command80Command palette / global search
--z-debug90Dev tools · debug overlays

Why tooltip (30) is above dropdown (20). A tooltip can emerge from a dropdown item — for instance, hovering a "Free tier — limits apply" link inside a Pricing dropdown reveals a tooltip. The tooltip must sit above the dropdown panel it's emerging from.

Touch targets — 44×44 minimum (WCAG 2.1 AAA)

Every interactive element has at least 44×44 px of hit area on touch devices. The visible element can be smaller; what matters is the area that registers a tap. Expand hit area via ::after { inset: -X } when the visible element stays small. Token: --touch-target-min: 44px.

Browser polish — 11 rules

RuleWhy
text-rendering: optimizeLegibilitySharper kerning on display headings
-webkit-text-size-adjust: 100%Suppresses iOS Safari's auto-resize on landscape rotation
font-size: 16px on inputsiOS auto-zooms when focused input is <16px — real bug fix
spellcheck="false" + autocomplete="off" on demo inputsDocs inputs are non-data. Real product forms set per-field.
user-select: none on buttons + line numbersStops accidental selection on mis-drag
Universal [disabled] stateOpacity 0.4 + pointer-events: none — one rule, all buttons
@media (hover: hover) wrap on decorative hoversTouch devices fire sticky :hover on press — wrap prevents stuck states
-webkit-tap-highlight-color: transparentReplaced with 96ms scale(0.985) on .btn:active
font-variant-numeric: tabular-numsFixed-width digits on metric grids, line numbers, timers
IntersectionObserver pause on tickersPauses ticker rows when scrolled offscreen — saves GPU
Two-tier ::selectionOrange for headings + titles; soft grey for body

Surface-variant convention

Every component ships in --on-dark and --on-light form (two named exceptions: code block always-dark; WebGL hero variants dark-only). Modifiers compose with existing tone / fill variants. Section flips work because every component binds to scoped CSS variables that rebind under .bk-section--dark / .bk-section--light / .is-flipped-*.

Previous← Logos & lockups NextBrand & voice →
Foundation / Brand & voice

Brand & voice

Infrastructure-confident, editorial, declarative. The voice reads like an engineer wrote it for other engineers, but it was edited by someone who reads The Economist.

Tone

  • No exclamation marks. No emoji. Anywhere. Period.
  • Sentence case for everything readable (display headings, body, list items, card titles). Title Case is reserved for two places: section labels in the nav ("Platform", "Agents", "Pricing"), and product / tier names ("Free", "Usage-Based", "Committed Annual").
  • UPPERCASE + 0.2em letter-spacing lives only in mono chrome — section codes (N/01, V/01, 02 / THE PLATFORM), badge labels, status text, footer meta. Never for prose.
  • Second person for product-facing copy ("you", "your"). Never "we" except in the footer.
  • Active voice. Always "the agent searches", never "is being processed by".

Lexicon — use these words

infrastructure-grade, scaffolding, layer, primitive, queryable, multimodal, runtime, native, scaled, deterministic, programmatic, perception layer, agentic, index, embed, ingest.

Lexicon — never use

seamlessly, magical, unlock, supercharge, revolutionary, world-class, cutting-edge, AI-powered, leverage, robust, enterprise-grade. These read as marketing pap. The VideoDB voice is technical confidence; these words signal absence of confidence.

Microcopy patterns

  • Button labels: sentence-case Geist label-md 14 / 400 / 20px. One word ideally — "Subscribe", "Get access", "Notify me". Two if needed. Never uppercase mono.
  • Field labels: sentence-case Geist 12 / 500. Short — "Name", "Email", "Project description".
  • Mono chrome: JetBrains Mono uppercase with letter-spacing: 0.2em. Does the "technical metadata" semantic work.
  • Numerical facts: integers with units inline (2.4M, 120ms, 38, ∞). The ∞ symbol is rendered in brand orange — the only orange numeral in the entire system.

Canonical tagline

Data infrastructure for video, built for machines and agents.

Use in chrome (footer, OG metadata, alt text) and as a reusable section ending pattern in editorial.

Previous← System rules NextButton (Atoms) →
Atoms / Pill

Pill

Tab pill — the segmented-control primitive. Identical box dimensions across selected and unselected (every pill carries a transparent border so the 1px never causes height drift).

Variants

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Selected state is solid; unselected is subtle. Selected pill inverts the surface — solid white on dark, solid charcoal on light. Unselected sits at a low scrim.

Transparent border on all pills. Locks the box height so swapping selected state never shifts layout by 1px.

Tablist composition

Three or more pills form a tab-group. Wrap them in a parent with role="tablist" and an aria-label. Each pill carries role="tab" + aria-selected="true|false". Exactly one tab carries aria-selected="true" at any time — no empty-state tablist.

Keyboard pattern. Left / Right arrows move focus between tabs; Home jumps to the first tab, End to the last. Tab key moves focus out of the group to the next focusable element (standard tablist behavior — Tab doesn't cycle within tabs).

Use a Mode toggle for 2 options. Below three, switch to Mode toggle. Above seven, switch to a select or autocomplete pattern.

Tag chip

Mono uppercase 11px chip with 4px small-rounded radius. Used for metadata, tag groups, language indicators.

Variants

on-dark python latency
on-light python latency

Metadata-level signaling. Stay neutral — never use orange, color-coded chips, or filled variants. The system's only data-typing tag style.

Atoms / Status pill

Status pill

Card-footer indicator. Pill radius. The leading dot is always orange — the system's only orange numeral / glyph apart from the ∞ symbol.

Variants

on-dark Live · v2.4.0 Recommended
on-light Live · v2.4.0 Recommended

Save states

Use these semantic modifiers for compact editor / form save indicators. They describe the state in text first; colour and motion only reinforce it.

on-dark Unset Ready to save Saving
on-light Unset Ready to save Saving

Usage rules

Leading orange dot is the signature for live / status indicators. The dot stays orange regardless of pill variant — it's the "this is a status" semantic.

Orange variant is reserved for "Recommended" tier markers and similar focal labels. Use sparingly.

Save-state modifiers are ds-pill-status--unset, ds-pill-status--ready, and ds-pill-status--saving. Use them for local save state only; don't use them for uptime, release, or pricing labels.

Atoms / Mono badge

Mono badge

Dot pattern, punched through. Texture below, glyphs above. The radial-gradient dot field reads as texture across the badge; text sits on top with a multi-offset text-shadow halo in the section background color — preserving the pattern as continuous texture rather than blanking out whole rows.

Variants

on-dark N/01 V/01 · Storage V/02 · Divider Live · v2.4.0
on-light N/01 V/01 · Storage V/02 · Divider Live · v2.4.0

Usage rules

Section ID badges. Used as the section-code marker (e.g. N/01, V/02) at the start of folds. Not for general labeling.

Text-shadow halo matches the surface bg. On dark, halo is --neutral-dark. On light, halo is --surface-light. The halo punches text through the dot pattern continuously.

Bracket header

Signature pattern. Bracketed mono label + uppercase mono tag. Used inside pricing cards and compare cards.

Variants

on-dark
[$0 / MONTH]Free
[CUSTOM]Enterprise
on-light
[$0 / MONTH]Free
[CUSTOM]Enterprise

Square brackets are literal text — written as part of the label content, not generated via CSS. Preserves copy-pasteability.

Orange variant highlights the recommended / featured tier — pricing's "Enterprise" or the active row in a compare card.

Eyebrow

Variants

on-dark The Platform

Vertical bar bullet

2px × 16px solid bar. The bullet for every feature / comparison list. Never replace with disc, check, or hyphen.

Variants

on-dark
  • 5 GB storage

on-light

Previous← Eyebrow NextInput →
Atoms / Input

Input

Pill or card-radius text field. 16px font-size (avoids iOS auto-zoom on focus). Three states — default, focused, error. Pairs naturally with a primary button to form a subscribe / search / auth composition.

Default state

on-dark
on-light

Focused state

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

16px font-size minimum. Under 16px, iOS Safari auto-zooms when the input is focused — visible bug.

Pill radius for inline forms. Card radius (12px) for multi-field forms. Both share the same input atom; only the radius modifier differs.

Three states. Default, focused, and error each get their own preview. Error uses aria-invalid="true", helper text, and the shake animation.

Invalid state uses aria-invalid="true". The ARIA attribute is the canonical validation hook. It applies the error border and triggers a 120ms horizontal shake; remove it when the field becomes valid.

Form validation contract

Use aria-invalid="true" as the only field-level validation signal for .ds-input, .ds-textarea, and .ds-select. Put the human-readable message in a sibling .ds-helper.is-error. Do not add ad-hoc .has-error classes or inline red borders.

Focus halo

Keyboard focus uses the global :focus-visible orange halo. Inputs also set the border to orange. Static docs use .is-focused only to preview the focused visual without requiring keyboard interaction.

Error state

on-dark Blur the field to replay the invalid shake.
on-light Blur the field to replay the invalid shake.

Atoms / Field label

Field label

Sentence-case Geist 12 / 500. Short — "Name", "Email", "Project description". Sits directly above its associated input with 8px spacing.

Variants

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Always paired with an input. Field label without an associated input is a misuse — that's an eyebrow or helper text instead.

Sentence case, never UPPERCASE. Field labels are read at body cadence, not chrome cadence. Uppercase is the eyebrow's job.

Atoms / Radio

Radio

18 × 18 pill-radius radio control. Orange-500 fill when checked. Wrap the input inside its <label class="ds-field-choice"> so clicking the visible text also flips the control — every preview below uses that wrapping idiom.

Variants

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

One-of-many. Use radios when only one option in a group can be selected. For independent toggles, use Checkbox.

Always native <input type="radio">. Custom div radios break keyboard handling, form-submission, and screen-reader semantics.

Previous← Field label NextCheckbox →
Atoms / Checkbox

Checkbox

18 × 18 subtle-radius checkbox. Orange-500 fill + white tick when checked. Independent state — multiple checkboxes in a group can be active simultaneously.

Variants

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Many-of-many. Use checkboxes when each option is independently togglable. For single-choice, use Radio.

Subtle 4px radius distinguishes checkbox from radio at a glance — radius is the semantic differentiator.

Previous← Radio NextSelect →
Atoms / Select

Select

Card-radius dropdown with custom chevron caret (inline SVG, currentColor). Inherits input styling — same 16px font-size, same border, same focus ring.

Short option list

Three to four options. Common case — tier picker, environment switcher, sort key.

on-dark
on-light

Placeholder + longer list

Six to eight options with a placeholder-disabled first <option>. The placeholder option carries disabled selected so it shows on first render but can't be re-picked.

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Native <select>. Custom dropdowns break iOS keyboard, accessibility, and form submission. The custom chevron is purely visual; the OS picker stays native.

Caret is a CSS background-image, not the native arrow. Strip the OS arrow with appearance: none, then paint our chevron via inline-SVG background-image (currentColor-tinted on dark, charcoal on light). No JS, no extra DOM.

Three-to-eight options. Below three, use radios. Above eight, consider an autocomplete / typeahead pattern.

Placeholder option must be disabled. A selectable "Select…" placeholder is a dead value — disable it so the user can't submit the form in its placeholder state.

Previous← Checkbox NextTextarea →
Atoms / Textarea

Textarea

Multi-line input. Card radius (pill doesn't work multi-line). Vertical resize only — horizontal resize breaks the column.

Variants

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Vertical resize only. resize: vertical is the only allowed value — never both or horizontal.

Min-height 100px. Below that, switch to Input. Above 300px, consider a separate composer surface. Modal-context textareas drop to 80px to keep the dialog compact.

Pin font-family: Geist explicitly. Browsers default textareas to a monospace stack; the inherit chain doesn't carry from body reliably. Always set the family on the element so paragraphs in a textarea read at the same cadence as everything else.

Previous← Select NextHelper text →
Atoms / Helper text

Helper text

12px subtle text below an input. Carries hint, validation feedback, or a "no data submitted" demo note. Two semantic states — default subtle and error red.

Default · guidance

Low-emphasis hint that sits below an input. Tells the user what the field expects or what happens on submit.

on-dark We'll send a one-time confirmation
on-light We'll send a one-time confirmation

Error · validation

Same primitive with aria-invalid="true" on the input and is-error on the helper — the field gets the error border + shake, while helper text turns --color-error. Use on submit-fail or live-validation; never to scold the user for in-progress input.

on-dark Enter a valid email · we don't share addresses
on-light Enter a valid email · we don't share addresses

Usage rules

Use for guidance, not requirement. Required-field asterisks are forbidden — every visible field is required unless explicitly marked optional.

Error helper is red. Use is-error on helper text only; use aria-invalid="true" on the associated input for the same border and 120ms shake used by Atom/Input.

Previous← Textarea NextLoaders →
Atoms / Loaders

Loaders

Six loading-state primitives, all functional motion (exempt from the 200ms decorative cap). Dot loader is the brand-signature loader — a 7×7 grid driven frame-by-frame by a tiny JSON-coordinate engine. The others handle conventional UI loading states.

Dot loader · brand signature

7×7 grid, frame-by-frame from JSON. Three frame sets: wave (default, 130ms cadence), snake (130ms), pulse (220ms). The engine inserts 49 dot spans on first paint, then toggles .is-active on the indices listed in the current frame. aria-label required.

on-dark · wave
on-light · wave
on-dark · snake
on-light · snake

Dot loader · orange pulse

Same engine, brand-orange variant on both surfaces. Pulse frame set with 220ms cadence — radial expansion from the centre cell. Used for emphasis loads where the orange should read as the focal action (auth callbacks, indexing completion, agent run starts).

on-dark · orange pulse
on-light · orange pulse

Status dot pulse

8px brand-orange circle, 1.2s pulse loop. Used in code-block status bars + live-feed indicators. Paired with an uppercase mono label like "Live", "Streaming", "Active". Pulses opacity + scale together so the dot reads as a heartbeat, not a strobe.

on-dark Live
on-light Live

Inline spinner

22px circular SVG, 2px stroke, currentColor, 800ms spin. Surface-aware via context — uses currentColor so it inherits from parent text. Use inside primary buttons for "submitting" state, or standalone for fast indeterminate fetches.

on-dark
on-light

Skeleton shimmer

Block with diagonal gradient shimmer sweeping every 1.6s. Content-loading placeholder. Reserves layout space while content loads — prevents the page from collapsing-and-expanding when async data arrives.

on-dark
on-light

Linear progress · indeterminate

2px tall track + orange-fill 30% segment sweeping on a 1.4s loop. Page-load top-band style. Determinate (fixed completion %) is a separate composition — this is the indeterminate primitive.

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Pick one per surface. Don't stack a spinner inside a skeleton or vice versa — the visual noise undoes the purpose.

Functional motion exempt from 200ms cap. These animations loop continuously by design — see Motion / functional.

aria-label required on dot loader. Screen-reader users need to know what's loading. Other loaders inherit semantics from their context (button-in-progress state, etc.).

prefers-reduced-motion: spinner and dot-loader fall back to static final-state via the global CSS rule. Skeleton + progress lose their sweep animation but stay visible as the placeholder.

Molecules / Section heading

Section heading

* What changed in v2.1 New --split modifier — asymmetric heading-left + lead-right (1.4fr / 1fr, baseline-aligned). Collapses to single column below 900px. Title clamp() applied (see Typography). Mobile lead size 18→16.

The canonical opener for every section / fold on a marketing page. Eyebrow + display heading + lead paragraph, stacked at 16px gap with a 720px max-width on the body copy. The most-used molecule in the kit — every fold starts with one.

Variants

on-dark
The Platform

Video as a queryable table.

VideoDB explodes every video into multidimensional indexes — visual objects, spoken words, timecoded moments — so agents can query specific seconds the same way they query rows.

on-light
The Platform

Video as a queryable table.

VideoDB explodes every video into multidimensional indexes — visual objects, spoken words, timecoded moments — so agents can query specific seconds the same way they query rows.

Usage rules

One per section. A section that opens with two competing headings reads as two sections smashed together. If you need two, you need two sections.

Lead is optional but recommended. Eyebrow + title alone works for short scannable sections (FAQ, footer); longer narrative folds need the lead to set context.

Body copy capped at 720px. Beyond ~80 characters per line, readability collapses. The molecule enforces this — don't override.

Previous← Loaders (Atoms) NextStat block →
Molecules / Stat block

Stat block

Big mono numeral + uppercase mono label. The metric primitive — three or four of these in a row makes a complete social-proof / capability strip. Value sits at 56px Geist 300 with tabular-nums (so digits don't dance when you swap them); label sits below in the system's Eyebrow cadence.

Default

Standard stat with neutral value color.

on-dark
2.4M Hours indexed
10× Faster than blob storage
on-light
2.4M Hours indexed
10× Faster than blob storage

Orange highlight

Adds .ds-stat__value--orange to focal stats. Use sparingly — one orange stat in a strip of four reads as the headline number; multiple oranges dilute.

on-dark
99.99% Indexing uptime
on-light
99.99% Indexing uptime

Usage rules

Use tabular-nums. The atom enforces font-variant-numeric: tabular-nums so digits have equal advance width — critical for stat strips where animated counters need to land cleanly.

Count-up is opt-in. Add data-ds-count-up to .ds-stat__value when the number should animate once on viewport entry. The parser preserves suffixes and formatting like 2.4M, 99.99%, 3,400+, and 10×.

Three to five per row. Below three, use inline copy. Above five, the eye starts skipping numbers.

Label stays short. Three to five words. The label is the unit / context for the number — not a marketing sentence.

Previous← Section heading NextCTA pair →
Molecules / CTA pair

CTA pair

* What changed in v2.1 Stack-and-fill mobile behavior: .ds-cta-pair inside .ds-cta-band auto-converts ≤768 — column flex, align-items: stretch, width 100%, gap 12, child buttons full-width padding-block 14. New opt-in modifier .ds-cta-pair--stack-mobile for using the same behavior outside the closing CTA band.

Primary + Ghost button paired side-by-side with a 12px gap. The canonical hero and section-closer conversion pattern: a focal primary action ("Get API key") and a softer companion ("Read docs"). The .ds-cta-pair wrapper exists to lock the gap so the pattern stays consistent across pages.

Default

Primary action on the left, ghost companion on the right. Convention: the primary is forward motion (sign up, get key); the ghost is exploration (docs, demo, learn more).

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Always Primary + Ghost. Never Primary + Primary (competing CTAs) or Primary + Secondary (Secondary is for paired-CTA states inside forms, not hero conversion). Ghost is the established companion.

Primary on the left. Reading order matters — the focal action leads, the companion trails. Centered alignment (in heroes) keeps Primary first regardless of LTR/RTL.

Wrap on narrow viewports. Below ~480px the pair wraps to stacked — the flex-wrap: wrap on the container handles this. Don't override.

Previous← Stat block NextCopy snippet →
Molecules / Copy snippet

Copy snippet

A single-line CLI / code sample with an inline copy-to-clipboard button. The developer-marketing essential — every "pip install videodb" gets one of these. Mono 13px text in a 12px-radius surface; copy button uses the same uppercase mono pattern as anchor-pill buttons. A $ prefix is added via ::before on the line span (literal text is the command only — keeps copy-paste clean).

Default

The inline / tutorial variant. Neutral mono text in the surface's text color.

on-dark
pip install videodb
on-light
pip install videodb

Install variant

Add .ds-snippet--install for the install-page-hero treatment: larger 18×22 padding, 14px font size, brand-orange command text. The signal that says "this is the canonical install command" on a marketing / Get-Started fold.

on-dark
curl -fsSL https://artifacts.videodb.io/call.md/install | bash
on-light
curl -fsSL https://artifacts.videodb.io/call.md/install | bash

Usage rules

Single line only. For multi-line code use the Code block organism. Copy snippet is the inline-CTA pattern — designed to feel lightweight enough to drop into a hero or section closer.

Default for inline / tutorial use; --install for the install-page hero. The install variant's orange command text is the focal signal — don't reuse it for regular code lines or the orange loses its semantic.

One install variant per page. The --install modifier carries the "canonical install command" weight; two oranges on one page dilute it.

Prefix is decoration. The $ is painted by CSS so the underlying text is just the command — clipboard copy operations get clean text without the prompt symbol.

Copy button hover-tints orange. The whole signature is the orange flash on hover — preserved on both surfaces so the affordance is recognisable across the site.

Feedback on click. JS swaps the button label from "Copy" → "Copied" for 1.2s after a successful copy. Without that feedback, users press the button twice unsure if it worked.

Previous← CTA pair NextTag list →
Molecules / Tag list

Tag list

Row of Tag chip atoms with 8px gap and flex-wrap. The card-meta pattern — used in article cards, blog topic strips, capability badges, and anywhere a piece of content carries multiple short labels. The wrapper codifies the gap so multiple tag lists don't drift visually across pages.

Default

Static, non-interactive tags. The most common variant — labels that describe the content rather than filter it.

on-dark
python indexing latency agents
on-light
python indexing latency agents

Usage rules

Two to six tags per list. Below two, use inline text. Above six, the meta row competes with the content — switch to a single "+ N more" affordance.

Tags stay neutral. No orange tags, no color-coded categories, no icons inside chips. Tag chip is the system's only neutral data-typing surface — the consistency is the point.

For interactive filter chips, switch to Pill + Tablist composition. Tag chips look passive on purpose; if a user can click them to filter content, the visual language should be Pill's "selected vs unselected" affordance, not Tag chip's quiet neutrality.

Previous← Copy snippet NextForm field →
Molecules / Form field

Form field

Field label + Input + optional helper text, stacked vertically. The atomic unit of form composition — every input the user touches sits inside one of these. 8px gap between label and input; 6px gap between input and helper.

Default

Standard field with label + input. Used in 90% of forms.

on-dark
on-light

With helper text

Adds a hint or constraint below the input. Common for password rules, format requirements, or "we'll send a confirmation" reassurance.

on-dark Lowercase letters and dashes only · 3–32 chars
on-light Lowercase letters and dashes only · 3–32 chars

Error state

Failed validation. Input uses aria-invalid="true" for the red border + shake; helper text turns red and explains the fix.

on-dark Lowercase letters and dashes only — strip caps and the bang
on-light Lowercase letters and dashes only — strip caps and the bang

Usage rules

Always label. Placeholder isn't a label — it disappears on input. The Field label atom is mandatory.

One field per row by default. Two-up layouts (name + email, city + zip) are fine when fields are obviously paired; never stack three fields horizontally.

Required fields aren't marked. Every visible field is required unless explicitly noted optional in the label or helper.

Previous← Tag list NextSubscribe band →
Molecules / Subscribe band

Subscribe band

Inline email-capture composition: label + pill input + primary button + helper text. The canonical newsletter / waitlist surface — used in section footers, modal CTAs, and the homepage subscribe block. 12px gap between elements; input and button live on one row, helper sits below.

Default ds-subscribe-band

Two-line stack: label + (input · button), with helper underneath. v2.2.2 (c-089): the pill input radius is now baked into the canonical wrapper — every `.ds-input` inside `.ds-subscribe-band` auto-inherits the full pill radius so it visually pairs with the adjacent primary button. No `ds-input--pill` modifier required.

on-dark · ds-subscribe-band
Useful signal only · no spam · unsubscribe anytime
on-light · ds-subscribe-band
Useful signal only · no spam · unsubscribe anytime

Usage rules

Single field only. Subscribe band captures one email. If you need name + email or other fields, switch to a multi-field form inside a card.

Helper carries trust copy. "No spam", "unsubscribe anytime", or "weekly only" — the helper is where conversion friction is removed.

Confirm successful submits. Click moves through Sending, then Thank you with ds-btn--success-on-submit, then resets to the original label.

Pill radius is automatic in v2.2.2+. Use the .ds-subscribe-band wrapper and any `.ds-input` inside inherits the pill radius. The standalone .ds-input--pill modifier still exists for inputs outside this composition.

Previous← Form field NextMode toggle →
Molecules / Mode toggle

Mode toggle

Binary control with a sliding pill indicator. The two-button pattern for view-mode switches: list / grid, monthly / annual, light / dark, code / preview. Sliding indicator moves on a 260ms ease — the only motion in the system that responds directly to a click. Not for tablists with three or more options — see the Pill atom's Tablist composition section for those.

Variants

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Binary only. Two options. Adding a third turns it into a tablist — switch to the Pill atom's Tablist composition pattern.

State is visible. The sliding pill makes the current selection obvious without inspecting which button is darker — important when the two icons look similar.

Slider position via CSS custom props. JS reads each button's offsetWidth + offsetLeft on click and writes --ds-slider-w + --ds-slider-x on the parent so the slider transitions to the new position.

Previous← Subscribe band NextCode tab pills →
Molecules / Code tab pills

Code tab pills

Compact tab-pill group designed to sit above a code block. Mono labels, 12px font, 6px gap, white-on-charcoal selected state. Used to switch runtime (npx / pip / typescript), framework (react / vue / svelte), or example (basic / advanced / streaming).

Default · on-dark

Code blocks live on dark surfaces by convention — this molecule reflects that. A separate on-light variant exists for inline code in light-surface articles (see Variants below).

On-light variant

Not in the cleanup source — added here for parity with the rest of the system. Used inside light-surface tutorials or article code samples.

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Pair with a code block. Code tab pills aren't a standalone primitive — they're the chrome that switches a code-block's contents. See Code block for the composed organism.

Default to the most-popular runtime. npx for JS, pip for Python, react for framework switchers — the option a new visitor most likely already has installed.

Switch is instant. No fade, no slide — the code-block content swaps in < 50ms. Tab pills exist to feel like a fast filter, not a transition.

Previous← Mode toggle NextSurface toggle →
Molecules / Surface toggle

Surface toggle

Sun / moon button pair that flips a section's surface between dark and light. Sits absolute top-right of any flippable section. 32×32 icon-only buttons in a 4px-padded pill container.

Variants

on-dark
on-light

Usage rules

Place absolute top-right of the section. The toggle is chrome for that one section, not a global control. position: absolute; top: 24px; right: 24px is the canonical placement.

Activate on click. Click keeps mouse, touch, keyboard, and assistive tech paths aligned while the button pair updates is-active and aria-pressed.

Disable transitions during flip. Add a .is-flipping class to the section that suppresses all CSS transitions for one frame, so the colors swap atomically and don't crossfade through invalid intermediate states.

Molecules / Bracket head + tag

Bracket head + tag

The signature pricing-card header pattern — bracketed mono price on the left, uppercase tier-name label on the right, both inside the same Bracket header atom. This page documents the pattern of "use these two parts together as a unit" rather than introducing a new primitive; both the __label and __tag spans are part of the Bracket atom and flip to orange together via the --orange modifier.

Note: the "tag" half is plain mono text inside the Bracket atom — it is not the chip-styled Tag chip atom (which carries a border + background). If you need a real chip beside a bracket, compose .ds-bracket + .ds-tag-chip manually.

Default

Standard tier marker. Mono price in brackets, tier-name chip beside it.

Featured (orange)

Recommended / featured tier marker. Both the bracket and the tag chip flip to orange together — they're a single semantic unit.

on-dark

Usage rules

One orange variant per pricing surface. The featured tier is one — competing oranges in the same compare row dilute the recommendation.

Brackets are literal text. Written as part of the label string, not generated via CSS. Preserves copy-pasteability and search.

Use only as a pair. If you find yourself wanting just the bracket or just the tag, use the Bracket header or Tag chip atom directly — this molecule exists to express the unit.

Tier finder

Slider-driven tier picker. The user drags the slider, the active marker updates, and the stat panel below recomputes (storage / API calls / support level). Pairs with the Pricing card row when "which tier fits me" is a real question — usage-based pricing models especially.

Usage rules

Pair with Pricing card, don't replace it. Tier finder is the secondary, "size me up" affordance. The pricing cards above it are still the source of truth for what each tier includes.

Always render an active state on first paint. Default to the most-common tier so the stats panel reads as filled-in rather than empty.

Selected tier price is orange-mono. The price subtitle is the only orange text in the card chrome — it's the "answer" the slider just gave the user, so it gets the focal color.

Fill width via CSS custom prop. The orange track-fill width is set via --ds-tier-fill. JS updates the prop + the active marker class + the stat values on slider change so the transitions run in CSS, not in script.

Usage rules

Stack vertically in a single column. Build stories are long-read articles; the eye scans down a column of meaty cards, not across a grid. Two-column grid is fine on very wide layouts but reads better as a stack.

Kicker carries the build identity. Format: How I built · <Author>. The mono-uppercase eyebrow tells the user "this is a builder talking" before they read the title.

Title size sits between Content card and Article hero. 20px Geist 500 with tight letter-spacing — bigger than feature-card titles so the build story feels substantive, smaller than article-hero so the card still reads as a list entry.

Arrow is top-right corner, not inline. Anchoring the arrow to the corner (vs at end of title row) keeps the card's content column clean and gives the hover-rotate animation room to breathe.

Anywhere-click is the rule. Card wraps in <a>. The arrow is visual chrome — no nested-link a11y trap.

Organisms / Video embed

Video embed

Aspect-ratio-locked container for an inline video player. The iframe (or <video>) inside handles all player chrome — controls, captions, chapter UI, the videodb.io player frame. This organism only contributes the surface: 16:9 aspect, 16px radius, charcoal background, optional caption strip below.

Default

The container alone. In production, the inner element is an <iframe src="https://player.videodb.io/embed?v=…">; the docs show a static placeholder so the player chrome isn't loaded just to render the surface.

on-dark
on-light

With caption

An optional .ds-video-caption strip below carries title + timing in the uppercase-mono cadence. Use when the video sits inside an article body and the surrounding flow needs the caption as a metadata anchor.

on-dark
Demo · Building a query agent 02:18
on-light
Demo · Building a query agent 02:18

Usage rules

The iframe is the player. Don't reimplement controls, captions, or chapter markers on top of this container — the videodb.io player handles them all and stays consistent across embeds.

Aspect-ratio locked at 16:9. Override only when embedding a vertical-format video (then 9:16) or a square (1:1). The surface chrome should never stretch the player.

Max-width 960px. Above that the player becomes the focal element of the page; if you want that, wrap it in a hero composition instead of leaving it as a free-floating embed.

Caption is meta, not summary. Title + duration only — don't pack a description into the caption strip. If the video needs context, use surrounding article copy.

Organisms / Article TOC

Article TOC

Right-rail sticky navigation for long-form articles. Vertical list of section anchors with a 1px left border that thickens to 2px orange and the link nudges 2px right when the section is active. Scroll-spy via IntersectionObserver in production; static .is-active in the previews below.

Variants

on-dark
In this note Problem First, the Lambda boundary Then, compression negotiation The gotcha in testing What we changed
on-light
In this note Problem First, the Lambda boundary Then, compression negotiation The gotcha in testing What we changed

Usage rules

Active state from click, focus, or scroll-spy. Demo links update is-active and aria-current on click/focus. In production, use IntersectionObserver with rootMargin -15% 0px -70% 0px so the active section is the one currently in the upper-middle of the viewport.

One link per article H2. H3 subsections don't get their own TOC entries — they'd make the rail too dense to scan. If a section is so long it needs subdivision, break it into multiple H2s instead.

Always carries aria-label="On this page". Screen-reader users land on the nav landmark and immediately know it's the article's local TOC, not the site nav.

Dark is the canonical surface. Code reads as code with a syntax-friendly dark background; the light variant exists only for inline embeds where the article context demands it.

Status bar is optional. Use metrics status for live runtime indicators (Live · 120ms · v2.4.0). Use filename status for quickstarts and file-oriented examples (quickstart.sh). The ready dot reuses the Status pulse primitive.

Tab pills always lead with the most-popular runtime. npx for JS, pip for Python, react for framework switchers — the option a new visitor most likely already has installed.

Organisms / Code annotation chips

Code annotation chips

Orange-tinted chips pinned next to specific lines of a Code block. Used to call out a "← this is the new bit" marker — a streaming line, an async boundary, a latency landmark. Each chip carries a pulsing orange dot + an uppercase mono label.

Layout: .ds-code-annotation is a 2-column grid — the code block on the left, a flex-column rail on the right that holds the chips. Each chip's margin-top aligns it to its annotated line. Below 640px the rail collapses inline above the code so the per-line callout pattern falls back to a horizontal tag-list summary on phones.

Usage rules

One chip per concept. Two chips on the same line read as competing — spread them across distinct lines so each is the focal note for its row.

Vertical alignment via margin-top per chip. The first chip's margin-top equals the line-height × line number it annotates (relative to the top of the rail). Subsequent chips use their own margin-top to space themselves down the rail.

Same chip on both surfaces, slightly softer on light. The orange-tinted bg drops from 10% → 8% alpha on light so it doesn't dominate a white page. Border alpha softens too. The pulsing dot stays full orange on both.

Below 640px the rail wraps inline. Chips stack into a horizontal flex-wrap row above the code block. Order is preserved, vertical alignment is dropped — at phone widths the per-line callout pattern doesn't work and the chips function as a summary tag-list instead.

Organisms / Highlight

Highlight

Inline orange-marker emphasis for body copy. The background is a linear gradient (transparent on top, orange-22% in the lower half) so the mark survives line wraps cleanly without overflowing letter ascenders. Two opacity variants: default for editorial emphasis, lighter for search-match contexts.

Default · marker

The "this is the focal phrase" treatment. Use one or two per article max — the orange has to remain a noticeable signal.

Search-match variant

Softer opacity. Used when many phrases get highlighted in a body of text simultaneously (find-in-page results, code-annotation matches). The full-strength marker would create visual noise with five highlights in a paragraph; this variant scales.

Usage rules

Default is the focal-phrase treatment. One or two per article max. Highlight is a signal, not a decoration — overuse turns it into noise.

Use the search variant when count > 2. Five focal-marker highlights in a paragraph competes with the body copy; the lighter search variant lets the matches scan as a set.

Survives line wraps. The gradient paints the same band on every wrapped line — no offset, no clipping. This is intentional and is why a flat background-color isn't used.

Entry row

Editorial list-row pattern — the alternative to a card grid when an index needs to feel like a list of articles rather than a stage of cards. Kicker meta + title + excerpt on the left, arrow on the right. Hover lifts the title to orange and translates the arrow 4px right. Stack a list of these for the Field Notes / Engineering / Blog index pages.

Usage rules

Use when content density > card density. The Labs index with 20+ entries reads as overwhelming as a card grid; a list of entry rows scans linearly and lets the title carry the weight.

Title at 22px Geist 400. Same scale as a Content card title — entries and cards stay typographically aligned so a mixed Labs index (featured card + entry rows below) reads as one hierarchy.

Organisms / FAQ row

FAQ row

Native <details> Q+A using semantic disclosure rather than custom JS state. The summary is the question, the body is the answer. Toggle indicator is a 32×32 circle with a + / − rendered via two pseudo-elements; the vertical bar rotates 90° on :open for a smooth glyph swap. A list of these forms the FAQ section.

on-dark
How does VideoDB index footage?
Multimodal embeddings + scene-cut detection + transcripts, all aligned to a single timeline. Each visual object and spoken word becomes a row an agent can query by timestamp, speaker, or semantic match.
What's the storage and bandwidth model?
You pay only for hours indexed and bandwidth streamed — there's no per-second storage tax. Free tier covers 10 hours / month; the Usage tier is metered linearly past that.
Can I bring my own models?
Yes. Director (our agent framework) is model-agnostic — swap in your fine-tuned CLIP, Whisper, or scene-graph model via the SDK. We provide good defaults; you provide better ones when you have them.

Usage rules

Use native <details>. Built-in keyboard support (Enter / Space to toggle), screen-reader semantics, and stateful disclosure — all without JS. Custom toggle widgets break one or all of these.

One row open by default. Mark the first row's <details> with the open attribute so the user lands on a populated section, not an empty list. Avoids the "where do I click" moment.

Question stays under 12 words. Long questions wrap to two lines and the toggle floats out of vertical alignment with the text. Keep them as actual questions a user might type into search.

Answer caps at 720px. Multi-paragraph answers in a 1000px-wide FAQ row read as walls of text. The cap holds the line length in the readable zone.

Variant B · Ticker

Marquee of customer names scrolling horizontally. Use as a slim band above or below the fold when you need social proof to feel "alive" — for example, between a hero and a feature fold. Composes the shared .ds-marquee primitive (60s loop, pause-on-hover, offscreen pause).

Usage rules

Grid for permanence, Ticker for liveness. A hero or trust-fold above the headline reads as "established" with the static grid. A slim band running mid-page reads as "active" with the ticker. Don't use both on the same surface.

Use real logo SVGs in production. The text-only cells in these previews are placeholders so the layout reads without external assets. Replace with <img alt="…"> SVG logos per cell when shipping.

Six to twelve logos. Below six, the wall reads as sparse; above twelve, individual logos lose recognisability. If you have more brand assets, rotate them per page rather than packing them all in one wall.

Organisms / Metrics ticker

Metrics ticker

Horizontal marquee of uppercase-mono key facts about the platform. Live indicators reuse the Status pulse dot. Items pause on hover (so a reader can finish reading one) and auto-pause when the ticker scrolls off-screen (via IntersectionObserver — saves CPU and battery). Built on the shared .ds-marquee primitive that Testimonials ticker also uses.

Usage rules

Duplicate every item in the markup. The marquee animation translates the track by 50% — the duplicate set is what fills the second half so the loop reads as continuous. Mark duplicates aria-hidden="true" so screen readers don't announce each item twice.

Items are atomic facts. Each item is one short phrase: a metric, a version, a status. No paragraphs, no full sentences. The marquee is meant to be scannable, not readable.

One Live dot per ticker. The Status pulse reads as "this number is updating in real time." More than one live dot dilutes the signal — promote the focal metric and leave the rest static.

Pause-on-hover + offscreen-pause are required. Both are wired automatically through the shared .ds-marquee primitive (CSS for hover, JS for IntersectionObserver). Don't reimplement.

Usage rules

Pick by surface and density. Single-row ticker for a slim trust-band placement. Card grid for a dedicated testimonials fold (six cards, static, scannable). Two-row ticker for the "lots of voices, kinetic" treatment with hover-slows.

Tickers slow on hover, never stop. Single-row ticker pauses fully; two-row ticker slows to 18% via WAAPI playbackRate. Hard stop reads as broken; slow-but-moving lets the reader read while the system stays alive.

Three to six unique testimonials. Below three the loop reads as repetitive. Above six the testimonials cease to feel curated and start to feel padded. Quality > volume.

Engagement meta is real or absent. If you don't have hearts / comments / repost counts, leave them out — invented numbers undermine credibility.

Production data wiring

The card is data-ready. When the testimonials sheet lands, each row binds to one card with these hooks:

Whole card as link. Swap the wrapping <article> for <a class="ds-testimonial-card ds-testimonial-card--dark" href="…" target="_blank" rel="noopener"> — the whole card becomes clickable to the source post. Card styling, hover, and the orange-platform-icon-on-hover all work unchanged.

Avatar accepts initials OR a real photo. Default is initials text inside .ds-testimonial-card__avatar (the cards above use this). For real photos, put an <img src="…" alt="…"> inside the avatar div — it covers the circle via object-fit: cover and the initials underneath act as fallback if the image fails to load.

All other fields are text-only. Name, handle, body, and each meta-item count are plain text — paste straight from the sheet. The platform icon is an iconify-icon with icon="ri:twitter-x-line" or icon="ri:linkedin-fill" driven by the sheet's platform column.

Organisms / Carousel

Carousel

Manual prev/next scroller with CSS scroll-snap. Slides snap to start-align so the user always sees full slides, never partial ones. Prev/next buttons disable when the viewport hits either edge — the dead state signals "nothing more this way." Use for release notes, changelog entries, project highlights — anything where the user picks one item at a time from a finite set.

Usage rules

Manual, not auto-rotating. Auto-advancing carousels are nearly always wrong — the user loses track of what they're reading mid-rotation. Manual prev/next + scroll-snap puts the user in control.

Buttons disable at viewport edges. The carousel JS toggles disabled on prev/next when the viewport reaches each end. A grey-out tells the user "no more this way" without the buttons silently no-op-ing.

Scroll-snap does the snap. Each slide carries scroll-snap-align: start + the viewport carries scroll-snap-type: x mandatory. The button click just scrolls by slideWidth + gap; the browser handles the snap.

Usage rules

Compact for grids of 3+, Prominent for featured 2-up. Compact's mono slug is the readable identifier when the user is scanning across many. Prominent's separate name + org breakdown reads as a focal callout — use sparingly.

Anywhere-click is the rule. Whole card wraps in <a>. The "Open repo ↗" CTA on Prominent is visual chrome — it doesn't have its own click target. Avoids the nested-link a11y trap.

Language colour follows GitHub's convention. Python #3776AB, JavaScript #F7DF1E, TypeScript #007ACC, Go #00ADD8, Rust #DEA584. Don't reach for our brand orange — it conflicts with the orange "Open repo" CTA hover. The dot in Prominent uses brand orange because there's no CTA-orange to fight with on that card.

Stats are uppercase mono, lowercased units. "4.2k" not "4,200". Updates feel newsy in lowercase mono ("2h ago") sat next to uppercase counts ("4.2K STARS"). Single visual rhythm across both variants.

Usage rules

Pick by intent — Directory vs Editorial. Directory when the footer's job is wayfinding (most product pages, marketing pages with deep IA). Editorial when the footer is the brand-statement closer (single-narrative landing pages, "about VideoDB" page, manifesto-style content). Don't mix the two — a footer is one or the other.

Editorial prelude line is the page-finale moment. Used for the etymology line ("To see is to know"), the mission summary, or a single-sentence brand statement. Keep it under 8 words; the type scale (up to 96px) does the work, the words have to earn the size.

Compliance pills (Editorial) carry the same trust signal as the badge band (Directory) — just smaller. The 32×32 circular text pills are a compact alternative when the bottom row should read as a single dense strip with the copyright + status. Both treatments are valid; pick by visual weight desired at the page bottom.

Status pulse is opt-in on Editorial. Drop the .ds-footer__status block if the page doesn't surface system status. Don't fake it — link the status indicator to a real status page when shown. Pulse is green (#2ECC71) for operational; respects prefers-reduced-motion by halting the animation.

Columns are flexible (both variants). Swap labels and link counts as IA evolves. Each column maps cleanly to one nav category — the example uses Product / Developers / Company / Legal (Directory) or Contact / Products / Resources / Info (Editorial), but the structure holds for 3 columns + a wider brand block, or 4 columns with mixed sizes. Don't go past 4 columns — at 5+ the labels start fighting for scan width on tablet.

Compliance row is non-negotiable. The badges live at the bottom always. If you're shipping a footer without compliance badges, you're shipping the wrong organism — use a plain <footer> with a meta strip and call it done.

Compliance badges (Directory) use bg-matched variants. Dark surface uses *-dark-bg.png, light surface uses *-light-bg.png. Same logo, two crops — the badge artwork is pre-treated so it reads on the target surface without filter trickery. Default opacity 0.7 lifts to 1 on hover.

Legal strip is mono-uppercase + 0.14em tracking. Same cadence as Customer-wall captions and Repo card meta — one shared mono-uppercase voice for service info / counts / version strings across the system.

Background is --neutral-darker on dark. One step darker than the page surface so the footer reads as a discrete chrome plate when the page ends, not a continuation of the section above it. Light surface stays pure white for the same separation against tinted page sections.

Responsive collapse. Nav grid drops from 4 columns → 2×2 at 900px; brand block stacks above the nav at 768px. Editorial prelude type ramps down via clamp() on narrow viewports. Compliance band / bottom row wraps naturally — the badges (or pills + status) just flow to a new row.

Motion / Atoms / Vocabulary

Motion atoms

Shared vocabulary for animated visuals. Every Motion organism and Data Viz diagram in the system composes these primitives — connector lines, arrows, packet tokens, node containers, grid-frame textures — so motion pieces feel like members of the same family instead of bespoke one-offs. Documenting them as a single page keeps the vocabulary explicit, not a folk-tradition passed between designers.

Animated vs interactive — terms used across this section

TermDefinitionExamples in this system
AnimatedMotion happens autonomously — looping, time-based, scroll-revealed. The user does not drive it; the component plays itself.Particle dome, Ingestion pipeline MP4, .ds-ticker, .ds-dot-loader.
InteractiveMotion responds to user input — hover, click, focus, scroll position. The user drives it; the component reacts.Timeline scrubber (hover thumbs to scrub), Architecture flow (continuous + hoverable).
BothAuto-cycles when idle (animated) and overrides to a user-driven state when engaged (interactive).Timeline scrubber's default behaviour — autoplays across the 6 moments, snaps to whichever thumbnail the user hovers.

Every entry under Motion / Components, Examples, and Data Viz is marked with one of these three labels in its lead paragraph, so the consumption contract is unambiguous.

Connector line (.ds-motion-connector)

Hairline SVG <path> linking two nodes in a diagram or motion organism. 1.5 px stroke, rgba(255,255,255,0.18) on dark / rgba(0,0,0,0.18) on light. Always axis-aligned — horizontal or vertical only. L-bends are three consecutive axis-aligned segments (horizontal → vertical → horizontal), never a diagonal cut across.

on-dark · straight + L-bend + dotted variants

Dotted variant. Use a dashed stroke (`stroke-dasharray: 3 4`) for pending, optional, or derived connections — anything that isn't a primary data path. Solid stroke stays the default; dotted is the deliberate signal that the relationship is conditional or secondary. One dotted edge per diagram maximum; more than that dilutes the contrast.

L-bend rule. Three segments: horizontal-in → vertical-bend → horizontal-out (or vertical-in → horizontal-bend → vertical-out). Each segment changes one axis only. No diagonal interpolation — that breaks "packet rides the wire" if packets travel the path later.

Cap density. 8 connectors per diagram is the soft limit. Above that, edge crossings become hard to read at typical column widths.

Connector arrow (.ds-motion-arrow)

Small triangular polygon at the connector's terminus — points into the target node. Width / depth 8 px. rgba(255,255,255,0.5) on dark / rgba(0,0,0,0.5) on light. Always at terminus, never mid-path. Mid-path arrowheads imply two-way flow, which the system doesn't sanction at v0.1 — for bidirectional, use two separate connectors.

Packet token (.ds-motion-packet)

7 px orange dot that traverses connector paths. 6 px box-shadow glow (rgba(242,78,30,0.55)). Centred via transform: translate(-50%, -50%) so positioning coordinates set the dot's centre, not its top-left corner.

on-dark · packets traversing connector

Motion rule. Packets traverse axis-aligned segments only — no diagonal interpolation between path waypoints. On an L-bend: travel horizontal segment, change direction at the bend, travel vertical segment, change direction, travel final horizontal segment. Each change keeps either x or y constant during the segment.

Stagger. Multiple packets on the same path stagger their begin times (typically 0.8 s apart on a 2.4 s cycle — three concurrent packets evenly spaced). Looks like continuous flow without obvious "frame 1, frame 2" beats.

Reverse direction. For outputs flowing right-to-left, use keyPoints="1;0" keyTimes="0;1" calcMode="linear" on the animateMotion — same path, opposite direction.

Node container (.ds-motion-node)

The atomic unit of a diagram. Hairline rectangle (1 px border, 4 px radius) holding two stacked text lines: a JetBrains Mono uppercase eyebrow (9 px, letter-spacing 0.15 em) and a Geist label (14 px, weight 500). Two variants:

  • Default — neutral hairline border rgba(255,255,255,0.4), ultra-subtle fill rgba(255,255,255,0.02). The "context" nodes.
  • Focal — orange border (1.5 px var(--orange-500)) + orange-tinted fill rgba(var(--orange-rgb), 0.05). The system's "VideoDB" position in any diagram. One focal node per diagram.
on-dark · default + focal variants

HOVER EITHER NODE TO INSPECT

Grid frame texture (.ds-motion-grid-frame)

Dotted-grid background pattern for thumbnail / preview containers. radial-gradient(rgba(255,255,255,0.07) 1px, transparent 1px) at 12 × 12 px tile size — reads as a quiet machine-grid surface, brand-consistent with the engineering-documentation voice. Used currently in the Timeline scrubber thumbnail cells; available to any motion piece needing a "frame placeholder" texture.

on-dark · 200×120 thumbnail with grid-frame texture

Note for future. If more textures emerge (cross-hatch, grain, stipple), promote this to a top-level Patterns & textures library section parallel to Motion / Illustration / Data Viz. For now, this single texture lives here as a Motion atom.

Usage rules

Compose, don't reinvent. If a new Motion organism needs a labelled box, use the Node container atom. A flow line — Connector line. A traveling indicator — Packet. Introducing one-off variants of these breaks the family resemblance the vocabulary is designed to enforce.

Orange is reserved. Orange fills appear only on Packets (always) and on the Focal node (one per diagram). Connectors, arrows, default nodes, and background textures stay neutral. Two orange focal elements per diagram fights for the eye; one wins.

Atoms aren't standalone components. These primitives compose into Components (e.g., Architecture flow uses Nodes + Connectors + Arrows + Packets) and Examples (Ingestion pipeline does too, baked into MP4). Don't put a bare Packet on a page — it would read as a tiny orange dot with no context.
